name: Primordial Origins
tagline: Before the gods, before Olympus — there was Chaos.
description: The first beings simply come to be: Chaos (a yawning gap), then broad-breasted Gaia, misty Tartarus and Eros. From Chaos come Erebus and Night, and from them Aether and Day. No one rules yet; the cosmos is still taking shape.

name: Primordial Generations
tagline: Earth bears Sky, and Sky lies upon Earth.
description: Gaia bears Uranus (Sky) and Pontus (Sea) on her own, then with Uranus produces the twelve Titans, the one-eyed Cyclopes and the Hundred-Handers. Uranus hides his most fearsome children inside the earth, and Gaia plots against him.

name: Age of Titans
tagline: A son's sickle ends one reign and begins another.
description: Cronus, youngest Titan, castrates Uranus and takes power. From the blood and foam come the Furies, the Giants and — in Hesiod's account — Aphrodite. Warned that he too will be overthrown, Cronus swallows his children by Rhea, until Rhea hides the infant Zeus on Crete.

name: Titanomachy
tagline: Ten years of war for the rule of the cosmos.
description: Zeus frees his swallowed siblings and wars on the Titans from Olympus while they hold Mount Othrys. The freed Cyclopes forge his thunderbolt and the Hundred-Handers turn the battle. The defeated Titans are bound in Tartarus.

name: Olympian Age
tagline: Zeus rules, and the world is divided by lot.
description: Zeus defeats the monster Typhon, the three brothers divide sky, sea and underworld, and Zeus fathers a new generation of gods. Prometheus' theft of fire and the abduction of Persephone belong here: the gods' order is fixed, and mortals find their place within it.

name: Age of Heroes
description: Hesiod's race of heroes, the 'demigods': Heracles and his labours, Jason and the Argonauts, the wars at Thebes. Gods intervene directly in human affairs and often father children with mortals.

name: Trojan War
tagline: A judgement, an abduction, ten years before Troy.
description: The Judgement of Paris leads to Helen's departure for Troy and a Greek expedition under Agamemnon. The Iliad narrates a few weeks of the tenth year; the sack of the city is told in other poems. In MYTHOS the war is the hinge: a myth in this sequence, and separately a debated archaeological question on the historical track.

name: Heroic Aftermath
description: The returns (Nostoi) of the Greek leaders: Agamemnon murdered on arrival, Menelaus delayed in Egypt, and Odysseus wandering for years before he reaches Ithaca. With them the age of heroes closes.
